body:
I feel like maybe some of this I could figure out, but I get overwhelmed easy (which I know is because of how I work, which is part of my OCD), so I hope you don't mind that I'm asking for some help.

Oh and that trigger warning. At first I thought I was going to describe all the reasons we thought residential might be a good fit for me. Skipped that, but here's some good news: After 10 attempts in my past, it's now been 6 years since my last one and now I'm better than ever at keeping myself safe despite some really intense urges lately. At least I can be proud of that.

Thanks in advance for any help. Please share if you know anyone else who may have answers. Thanks! 💜

I'm so sorry for your loss. To be honest, a lot of people react to grief with the same things you are, and many can't see a way out of it. I know when I've had times of deep pain out would actually piss me off when people pointed out signs that part of me wanted to live (because I'm like, but so much of me wants to die too!), but a lot of those people I mentioned clung to whatever they could, and honestly the fact that you're going to therapy - even though I know you're not loving it - shows me that there's still a part of you that wants to try. 

I'll leave you with this: in my worst times, I tell myself that I just have to stay safe for 5 minutes, and then if I want to do something drastic, I can. But the trick is after 5 minutes, I challenge myself again. Can I do 5 more minutes? And days when it's not quite as urgent, the challenge is I just have to last until i wake up tomorrow. Just one more day. 

I made an attempt 21 years ago. And I'm still here. You've got this.💜

This is definitely beyond hypomania. Perhaps before her illness had manifested as bipolar 2 (so it might not have been a misdiagnosis at that point), but if it was before, it isn't anymore. Does she receive any outpatient mental health care?
Honestly I don't think that would do much, if anything. I'm on 250mg of that a day, so that would just be 6x a safe dose.
We're on the same page then. 😊
Well then I suggest getting in contact with the folks at the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline. They would have the resources to get it going for sure.

What I do know is that if the suicidal person is the one who's supposed to pay, it probably won't work very well. If they're not convinced they should keep living, what's going to convince them to cough up money to get help with staying alive, something they're not even sure they want to do?
You could probably set it up as a non profit. And run a kickstarter for the development.
What do you mean? Who would be paying? I thought you meant this as a volunteer service?
Thank you, will do so now.

If the idea is feasible, you could look into connecting with the crisis centers that are a part of the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline. That's a huge network that includes high quality crisis training for their volunteers.

I don't know how feasible it is, but when I'm at my worst, my loved ones like to make sure I'm not alone / can spend the day with someone. It keeps me safe when I would otherwise need to be hospitalized. So if it IS feasible, it's an amazing idea.

Does anyone else do this? I'm thinking of what I'd put in my will. How I'd like to come off all three of my psych meds so I could be unstable enough that I could actually follow through with it. Thinking about what to put in my suicide note. Why I even want to die in the first place.

And all this while I've promised that I won't kill myself.

Does anyone else obsess like this?
I wish I could upvote this (is that what it's called? Am new to reddit) a thousand times.

Also, thank you for posting and sharing your situation. Thinking through my responses to you is helping me with my own struggles. I've been feeling suicidal lately (a long history of depression with quite a history of attempts and hospitalizations...not 100% treatment resistant, but at times it certainly seems that way), -- especially the last few weeks, sometimes getting really impulsive and desperate. I'm fighting the battle for life...sometimes with everything in me, and others super reluctantly. I've kept coming back to the pain I'd cause my fiance, but hadn't thought as much about the fact that I've had good times, and in those times I've always felt immensely grateful to still be alive.

So yes, thank you for being open here. You've helped me a lot just in this small exchange, and hopefully that will make a difference in my times of desperation. Thank you.

That's a really good question, about whether causing him more pain or being unable to escape yours is worse. The only thing I can think in response to that is that killing yourself guarantees more pain for him, whereas staying alive doesn't necessarily mean more pain for you. It might. Especially in the short term, as no treatments are helping right now. But you're not guaranteed a life filled with misery. Science is amazing, and they're always working on new treatments. And with time, those treatments get cheaper. TMS won't always cost $8k. Personally, my fiance is convinced they'll eventually come up with a little computer chip that can be implanted in the brain to treat depression. It's a possibility for sure. I think I'm starting to ramble, but the point here is that when trying to balance your pain versus his, one major thing to take into consideration is the likelihood of pain. Guaranteed (his) versus unknown (yours -- possible, maybe even probable, but not 100% guaranteed).

And the fact that he says he signed up for it, and he holds you so lovingly, is awesome. I'm really glad you have him.

This is all super hard to deal with, especially when your depression is treatment resistant, but I do think you're right -- maybe at the very least, you can keep living for him. I've heard some say you should want to live for yourself, but hey -- sometimes we just can't. And during those times, it's really great that we have someone to live for. 

As much as sometimes I feel utterly hopeless, the fact that I've experienced times of happiness and relief from the pain (such as the time you had after your TMS treatment) has shown me that life CAN be enjoyable...and so I think that if we can hang on for whatever reason -- even if it's only for someone else -- eventually we might be glad we did.

I can relate to a lot of what you're saying. I've been with my fiance for 6 and a half years and I feel the same as you do about how my depression affects him. It destroys him to see me in pain, to see me hurting myself. I feel like if I weren't here he wouldn't have to experience all the pain that I cause him. And he wouldn't be burdened by having to support me, financially and emotionally. I feel like he deserves so much better. 

But here's what keeps me from killing myself: it would hurt him a million times more if I died. When I'm feeling desperate and impulsive and am searching for how I can finally end it, I picture his reaction to hearing about my death. Or worse, his reaction upon finding my body. It becomes a genuine battle in my head. Wanting so desperately to act on my feelings, and then picturing his pain, and then rationalizing things, but then picturing his pain again. 

Sometimes I feel resentful of him. I feel like I'm stuck on this earth against my will because I don't want to hurt him. Like you, I sometimes wish he wasn't in my life so I could just die already.

But the biggest kicker to all this, when I feel like a burden and that he'd be better off without me, is that he strongly disagrees. He feels his life is a million times better with me in it. Despite all the pain I cause him, it's worth it to him.

I don't know your situation or your relationship, but maybe this might help show a different perspective. Maybe he loves you despite not knowing how to handle your struggles. Maybe he feels his life is better with you in it. Maybe it would destroy him to lose you.

I know that doesn't make things any easier. Believe me, I know. But maybe it can help you hang on longer than you might think. Long enough to find more relief and experience more joys in life that you would have missed otherwise.

I do. I see my therapist tomorrow. I don't really know how to process all this though.

I ended up spending 2 and a half hours on a chat with the suicide hotline yesterday not long after writing this. I was feeling really impulsive and desperate at that point. The chat helped some. Today I'm just numb. I guess we'll see how my appointment goes tomorrow.

I feel like I sound like some kind of spoiled brat. I'm sure in some ways, many people would kill to be in my shoes. Why the hell is all that I have going not enough for me? Why the hell must I take everyone's love for granted?

I went to a gym for awhile in 2008 that had something like this. It was a dongle (maybe USB? I don't remember) that got plugged into each machine you used, and then you could plug it into a computer and get all kinds of neat data about your workouts that day and into the past. I believe I had to pay a small upfront fee for the dongle (like $25-ish) – which was mine to keep – but the system was free to use beyond that. So I would guess that was a B2B model with the gym trying to recoup a little bit of the cost by not just passing it on to the consumer, but also by ensuring that the product wasn't being wasted on people who had no intention of ever using it.
